messages:
emily: FYI customer reported duplicate charges. They say our Python SDK retried a POST after a client-side timeout and the retry didn't include the idempotency header, so server processed the payment twice. Ticket #INC-4218.
prashant: Can you paste the minimal repro + sdk version and python version?
emily: SDK: redwood-python==0.14.2, Python 3.11.6. Using aiohttp + asyncio.wait_for around the call. Quick repro below.
emily: ```py
# simplified
import asyncio
from redwood import Client

client = Client(api_key='redacted')

async def charge():
    await asyncio.wait_for(client.payments.create(amount=100, idempotency_key='cust-123'), timeout=0.7)

asyncio.run(charge())
```
emily: Logs from the customer's side (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] -> POST /v1/payments 408 (timeout)
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] redwood-sdk retry attempt=1 reason=ClientTimeout backoff=0.6
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] outgoing request headers: { }
[2026-03-10T14:02:11Z] -> POST /v1/payments 200 id=pay_01abc
```
emily: The idempotency header (`Idempotency-Key`) is present on the first attempt but missing on the retry in their proxy logs.
katie: Are they using gunicorn/uvloop or process-based workers? Could be cancellation semantics leaking state.
emily: They run under uvicorn + uvloop, 4 workers. Happens intermittently on spikes.
prashant: I'm guessing asyncio.CancelledError from wait_for is being handled by our retry wrapper as a retriable error, but the request context (where we inject headers) is lost on cancel. That would explain header not being re-attached.
prashant: Repro attempt on my laptop with the snippet above -> I can repro ~30% of the time. Confirmed missing Idempotency-Key in second attempt.
prashant: Filing GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python/issues/4201 (title: "asyncio.wait_for cancel -> retry loses idempotency header").
support-bot: Created incident INC-2026-0310-2 and linked GH#4201. Assigned to @prashant. :rotating_light:
prashant: Quick mitigation ideas:
- ensure header injection happens on the prepared request object before awaiting user-level timeouts
- treat CancelledError from user timeouts as non-retriable by default (opt-in)

prashant: Plan: patch to attach idempotency header earlier + explicit handling for CancelledError. Will backport to 0.14.x and 0.13.x. Aiming for 0.14.3 tomorrow EOD and a hotfix branch for older releases.
katie: For customers hit by this, can we recommend a temporary workaround? maybe set a client-side header that the server checks for dedup or increase timeout and avoid wrapping with asyncio.wait_for.
emily: I suggested this workaround to the customer: set a server-side duplicate-detection key in the payload, or increase the wait_for timeout. They've paused payments for now.
prashant: Also adding an SDK option `preserve_idempotency_on_cancel=True` behind a feature flag for immediate relief.
anna: Customer update: they saw two charges for 3 customers. They're blocking until fix.
emily: I'll add detailed repro logs to GH issue and ask the customer for a sample trace.
prashant: Thanks. I'll post the fix PR and a release note. Follow-up in the issue. :pray:
emily: thanks all :thumbsup:
